newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-NOVOTNA WITHIN SIGHT OF WIN WHEN RAIN STOPS PLAY.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-NOVOTNA WITHIN SIGHT OF WIN WHEN RAIN STOPS PLAY.

text.p: Jana Novotna was serving for the match against Ai Sugiyama when rain again stopped play in the quarter-finals at the $450,000 Eastbourne women's grasscourt tournament on Friday.
Novotna, the second seed, was one set up and leading 6-5 in the second when the umpire called for the covers to be put on Devonshire Park's Centre Court after 74 minutes of play.
Natalia Zvereva of Belarus was leading Frenchwoman Nathalie Tauziat 6-4 5-7 2-1 in their quarter-final on Court Two when the rain started.
Thursday was scheduled to be quarter-final day at this traditional Wimbledon warm-up event but showers meant that only 41 minutes of play was possible.

Organisers were still hoping to finish the quarter-finals and semifinals on Friday, with the final scheduled for Saturday, but said the tournament could continue for an extra day on Sunday if necessary. The Wimbledon championships begin on Monday.
Defending champion Monica Seles was trailing Brenda Schultz- McCarthy 5-7 2-2 when play was abandoned on Thursday. Their quarter-final was scheduled to resume after the Novotna v Sugiyama match.
Eastbourne organisers scheduled Novotna on first on Friday because the Czech also had to fit in a doubles quarter-final, and possible semifinal, with American partner Mary Joe Fernandez.
Spaniard Arantxa Sanchez Vicario, the fourth seed, was due to play Romanian Irina Spirlea in the other singles quarter-final.

Sugiyama, who had trouble with cramp, was unable to cope with Novotna's skilfull serve-and-volley game in the first set and obligingly provided a double fault to give the Czech the second break which put her 5-2 up.
Despite her obvious irritation at the chilly wind, Novotna won the final game to love, ending with an ace.
Sugiyama coped better in the second set, breaking Novotna to go 2-0 up. But the Japanese woman hit a double fault in the next game, helping Novotna to break straight back.
Another break in the 11th game put Novotna 6-5 up but rain was already falling and at 15-15 in the next game play was called off. REUTER
